name: Estuary
premise: Quiet editorial competence. A deep green-teal ground against a bone paper, with the warmth coming from the paper rather than from a second expressive colour. Barishal sits in a river delta; an estuary is where fresh water meets salt, which is also what a studio serving two audiences in two scripts is doing. This is Direction A: the existing draft, corrected. One correction is substantive — the draft declares no accent at all, and a system whose accent equals its text colour cannot express a link, a selected row, or a primary action. A cyan-teal accent is therefore introduced: a near neighbour of the ground, discriminable from it, and still honouring 'no second expressive colour'.

ground.label: Estuary
ground.note: The ground, and the source of every surface tint and every text role.

accent.label: Tidewater
accent.note: A cyan-teal one hue-step off the ground. Carries links, focus and the primary action.
